blurb: `by Expired` sends an expired token, so it needs a route whose seam checks one: a `Bearer` or `Oidc` actor. A public route, or one guarded by a `Signature` actor, has no token to expire; for a `Signature` route `by Stale` sends a stale signature. An `ApiKey` actor's keys expire only when it declares a `ttl`; on an `ApiKey` route without one, give the actor a `ttl` or test it with `by Malformed`, `by Unknown`, `by Forged` or `by Revoked`. Drive a route guarded by a `Bearer`, `Oidc` or `ttl`-bearing `ApiKey` actor. See `bynk.test.nobody_needs_secured_route` for the same limit on `Nobody`.
summary: A case drives `by Expired` at an address that is not an http route with a `Bearer` actor (alone, or as a member of an actor sum) or an `Oidc` actor; it sends a correctly signed token whose `exp` has passed, so only a `Bearer` or `Oidc` seam, or an `ApiKey` seam whose actor declares a `ttl`, can refuse it (#3939).
